# DSH Studio v0.6.0

This release closes the gap between “installable” and durable operation: it
qualifies one complete upstream runtime set, makes Harness and plugin mutations
recoverable, adds secure multi-source discovery, persistent evidence and
workspace admission, and turns updater signing and artifact completeness into
formal release gates.

## Added

### Secure multi-source plugin discovery

- Discovery can switch between npm, a constrained DSH 1024Store adapter, and user-managed standard HTTPS catalogs.
- Custom endpoints must implement Schema 1.0.0 and can suggest only an exact npm name/version. Commands, scripts, paths, git specs, and build-permission hints cannot enter the installer.
- Requests reject credential URLs, non-443 ports, local/special-use addresses, DNS rebinding, cross-origin redirects, non-JSON and responses over 2 MiB. Installation still performs an independent npm manifest and Harness peer-range preflight.

### Recovery, diagnostics and workspace safety

- Harness installation uses durable staging/backup state and promotes a runtime only after version and entry-point validation.
- Plugin add, remove and offline import preserve a before-image; an interrupted package operation is recovered and reported on next launch.
- Persistent redacted logs, panic evidence, and one-click diagnostics now include runtime compatibility and recovery state.
- Windows workspace admission allows fixed NTFS/ReFS volumes and blocks network, removable, FAT/FAT32 and exFAT workspaces before Harness starts.

### Documentation, ecosystem and distribution

- Bilingual user, troubleshooting, architecture/trust-boundary, plugin/catalog, and community-conduct guides.
- The site now links upstream, catalog development and contribution paths while stating package-channel and Flatpak sandbox limits honestly.
- Generated WinGet, Homebrew, AUR and Flatpak validation jobs; the Flatpak manifest targets GNOME 49 and carries developer metadata and a real screenshot.

## Changed and secured

- Managed Harness is pinned to `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.8`, pnpm to 11.7.0, and Node to a minimum of 22.19. Stale or incomplete runtimes enter Repair instead of starting silently.
- Plugin installs use an npm-resolved exact version and reject incompatible or malformed peer ranges before mutation.
- A formal tag must match the application version and include detailed Chinese and English notes.
- Formal publishing requires Tauri updater signing and verifies the published cross-platform asset/signature matrix before `SHA256SUMS.txt` is generated. Windows Authenticode and macOS Developer ID signing/notarization/stapling are applied when their complete credentials are configured.

## Fixed and hardened

- Replaced the obsolete `0.0.1-rc.1` graph that requested the unpublished `@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker`, causing mirror 404s and misleading “No authorization header” output.
- Package-manager failure or forced shutdown no longer leaves half-written profile, node_modules or layer state.
- Initialized the rustls crypto provider on the independent catalog HTTPS path.
- Plugin details retain their selected source and exact version, preventing stale asynchronous results after rapid source changes.

## Install and update

Choose a Windows, macOS or Linux installer from Assets. Downloads can be checked
with `SHA256SUMS.txt`; in-app updates additionally verify the Tauri signature
with the public key embedded in Studio.

This release is not OS-code-signed because the repository does not yet have
Windows or Apple signing credentials. Windows may display an unknown-publisher
warning; on macOS, approve the app in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

If Environment reports Harness `0.0.1-rc.1`, `rc.6`, or another incompatible
release, use **Repair** to atomically replace it. Do not delete `~/.dsh` profiles.
